h: Birds, Beaches and a Proper Dorset Holiday
p: Lodmoor is a lovely corner of Weymouth to base a day around. Right alongside the aquarium is RSPB Lodmoor, a wetland nature reserve of reed beds, pools and marsh where you can spot wading birds and wildfowl from the paths, and it's free to wander. Bring a pair of binoculars and you can turn the morning into a mini wildlife safari, sea creatures inside and birdlife out on the marsh. The flat paths make it easy going for little legs and pushchairs too.

Kids tend to love the outdoor sections most, so it's worth checking on the day what talks are scheduled for the penguins and seals and planning your loop around them. Pack sun cream in summer and a waterproof the rest of the year, because you'll spend a good chunk of time in the open air, and there's not much shelter from that sea breeze.

Once you've finished, Weymouth has bags to fill the rest of your stay. Nothe Fort, a Victorian fort on the headland at the mouth of the harbour, is great for kids who like tunnels, cannons and ramparts. Over on the Isle of Portland, the red-and-white lighthouse at Portland Bill stands at the southern tip, with dramatic rocks and crashing waves. Chesil Beach, an extraordinary long shingle bank stretching west along the coast, is an unforgettable sight from the viewpoint on the way to Portland.

Weymouth's waters even hosted the sailing events at the London 2012 Olympics, and you'll still see plenty of sailing boats bobbing about in Portland Harbour on a breezy day. It's a properly outdoorsy part of the world, and the aquarium fits right in.
